find: if ('cssRules' in rule) walk((rule as CSSGroupingRule).cssRules, focusState);
replace: if ('cssRules' in rule) walk((rule as CSSGroupingRule).cssRules, underFocusState);
why: Descends with the state the parent inherited rather than its own, so `.a:focus { .b { display: none } }` reads as a plain `& .b` rule. A nested rule's selector never repeats its parent's state, which is why the state is carried down.
killedBy: computed-style-cache: the focus-state guard reports display set under a rule nested under a focus-state rule
